title: console: the localization fetch drops the `timezone` the server sends for the signed-in user, so no renderer can show dates in the user's or tenant's zone
body:
Ruled: 6030273339 · letter B · 2026-10-07T03:28Z
Blocked-by: #11758
Unlock-action: re-check PR #11729

Path: ② the capabilities an end user meets in the app — localization | 缺项 (no item asserts a date renders in the user's configured zone) | P2

Filed by the triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U`. It is the follow-up named in the ruling on objectui#11675 (B: formats follow the locale; `timezone` stays a live setting). ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

Triage: lands in `apps/console/src/LocalizationFetchProvider.tsx` (about `:108`) and `packages/i18n/src/LocalizationContext.tsx` (`LocalizationValue`) ⇒ `domain:ui`; rationale: the server answers `locale`, `timezone` and `currency` from `/api/v1/auth/me/localization` (objectstack `plugin-hono-server` `current-user-endpoints.ts`, #15387), and the console keeps only two of the three.

## Read on objectui `main`
`setValue({ currency: json.currency ?? undefined, locale: json.locale ?? undefined })`: the `timezone` in the same answer is dropped.

## Done when
- **Measure first:** whether any renderer already takes a zone from elsewhere (the session, or a per-field zone). Then the console carries the served `timezone` in its localization context.
- The central date formatters render in that zone when it is set, and the browser's zone stays the fallback when it is not.
- ⛔ No per-component special cases. The zone enters through the central formatters only.
- **Pins:** with the user's timezone set to a zone unlike the browser's, a datetime renders in the set zone; with none set, it renders in the browser's.

`bug` · `priority:p3` · `area:i18n` · `pm:queue`.
